timerApiObservation.interpretation: Both timer APIs are already function-valued at request. Their identities change from 1/2 to 3/4 before the first acquired callback, then stay stable for every remaining observed phase. This is an actual function replacement, not just a getter becoming a function.

sourcePath: AppNavigator imports auth/Supabase dependencies before CallProvider.
CallContext imports Daily, whose setupGlobals runs at module evaluation.
mechanism.dailyBehavior: @daily-co/react-native-daily-js 0.86.0 dist/index.js lines 112–119 replaces Android global timeout/interval functions with react-native-background-timer methods; setupGlobals is invoked at module load.
mechanism.registryBehavior: react-native-background-timer 2.4.1 index.js lines 80–84 clears only its own callback map. It cannot clear a handle previously scheduled by the RN timer registry.
mechanism.sdkBehavior: Verified auth-js 2.103.0 processLock creates its acquisition timer, awaits the previous operation, then calls the current global clearTimeout before invoking the acquired callback. A provider replacement across that await can leave the old timer alive even though the lock fulfilled.
controls: Android auth-first: callback runs once and fulfills, old-registry acquisition timer remains, then the exact 5000 ms warning is emitted when the synthetic deadline is delivered.
Android Daily-first: same callback/result, stable timer identities, no uncanceled callback and no warning.
iOS auth-first: Daily does not replace timeout functions; the original timer is canceled and no warning is emitted.
mechanism.conclusion: The source-level registry mismatch is reproduced and agrees with the emulator transition and approximately 5008 ms anchored warning. Direct runtime handle attribution is not available, so the next native run must verify the repaired order.
